Negative Appraisals.value: I used to be a happy person but now I am always miserable.
I feel like I don't know myself anymore
I feel that others can see what happened to me just by looking at me

vignette: Samantha, a 52-year-old Middle Eastern woman and project manager, has been profoundly impacted by her experience with terrorism. Her trauma began when she was caught in a violent attack on a public event. The sound of helicopters overhead, the flash of sirens, and the sudden appearance of armed police officers marked the moment of terror that left indelible impressions on her psyche. Since then, Samantha’s world has become a series of triggers that evoke vivid memories of that day. Every time she hears the whirring noise of a helicopter or sees a police officer in uniform, it transports her back to that terrifying event. The sound of helicopters alone makes her heart race and sends waves of anxiety through her body, as if the threat is imminent once more. Similarly, encountering any form of violence, even on television, brings back the overwhelming sense of danger and helplessness she felt during the attack. These triggers have significantly altered Samantha’s perception of herself and her place in the world. She has come to believe that she is no longer the person she used to be—someone who was happy and confident. Now, she feels like a shadow of her former self, always miserable and struggling to find joy or peace. Her sense of identity has been eroded by the traumatic event; she often wonders if she will ever feel like herself again. This loss of happiness and sense of self has led her to withdraw from social interactions and professional activities that once brought her fulfillment. Moreover, Samantha fears that others can see the trauma etched on her face or in her demeanor. She feels exposed, believing that her pain is visible to everyone around her. This belief makes it difficult for her to connect with colleagues at work, as she avoids eye contact and minimizes interactions during project meetings. Her husband has noticed a significant change in her behavior and mood, but Samantha struggles to articulate what she’s going through. The cumulative effect of these triggers and negative appraisals is that Samantha finds herself increasingly isolated both professionally and personally. At work, her avoidance behaviors have led to strained relationships with coworkers who see her as distant or unapproachable. She has missed important team meetings and project deadlines due to her anxiety and fear of encountering triggering situations. What finally brought Samantha to seek help was a series of near-misses where she nearly withdrew from her professional life entirely. The realization that her quality of life had deteriorated so dramatically, coupled with her husband’s persistent urging, pushed her to confront her fears and seek support. She is most afraid of losing her sense of self completely and becoming a person she no longer recognizes. However, she also hopes for a chance to reclaim some semblance of the happiness and confidence she once had before the traumatic event. In her current state, Samantha is acutely aware that something needs to change. The relentless cycle of triggers leading to negative appraisals has become unbearable, and she seeks help to break this vicious loop and regain control over her life.
